title: FIRST CONTACT: PRECISE DOCKING
subtitle: Measure the world, estimate the pose, and stop accurately at the glass calibration gate.
briefing: MISSION: stop stably at the glass calibration gate with zero collisions.
INSPECT: click the real 3D drive wheel and LiDAR. The wheel rolls without steering; LiDAR measures timed surface ranges.
PROVE: ROBOT declares arrival from its estimate; SIM independently verifies the physical stop.

shots.title: TRACTION STARTS AT THE CONTACT PATCH
shots.caption: A powered wheel rolls about one horizontal joint. Differential steering comes from left-right speed, never a hidden steering axis.

shots.title: PASSIVE SUPPORT STILL HAS PHYSICS
shots.caption: The caster swivels and rolls under measured load. Its pose comes from MuJoCo joints, not a draw-time animation.

shots.title: THE ROBOT MEASURES SURFACES
shots.caption: LiDAR begins at this configured optical frame. Ranges and acquisition timestamps become ROBOT observations only after RUN.

shots.title: YOUR PROOF: STOP AT THE GLASS GATE
shots.caption: ROBOT must decide from its own estimate. SIM truth remains outside the robot and independently judges the physical stop.

walkaround.title: DRIVE WHEELS / TRACTION
walkaround.lesson: Each drive wheel has one rolling joint. Differential steering comes from left-right wheel speed, so these wheels never swivel like steering wheels.

walkaround.title: PASSIVE CASTER / SUPPORT
walkaround.lesson: The caster carries load through two passive joints: a vertical swivel and a horizontal wheel roll. Neither joint is a drive command.

walkaround.title: LIDAR / TIMED RANGES
walkaround.lesson: The blue scanner reports ranges from this configured sensor frame. It measures surfaces; it does not reveal actor identities, scripts, or world truth.

walkaround.title: COMPUTE, CONTROL, AND CHASSIS
walkaround.lesson: The onboard robot turns timestamped measurements into estimates and commands. It reports arrival from its own estimate; the simulator judges the physical result separately.

experiments.title: WHAT CHANGES WHEN LIDAR UPDATES FIVE TIMES SLOWER?

prediction.question: What will change when LiDAR updates every 100 ms instead of every 20 ms?

choices.label: Both runs stay safe, but slower scans take longer and leave less clearance
choices.explanation: The two visible runs hold the world, robot, initial state, and random seeds fixed. Their recorded time and physical clearance decide whether this tradeoff occurred.

choices.label: The two runs finish with effectively the same time and clearance
choices.explanation: Equivalent means both measured differences remain inside the experiment's declared tolerances.

choices.label: The slower scan run collides or fails the safety gate
choices.explanation: Collision, timeout, incomplete objectives, or rejected physical arrival makes the slower run unsafe.

running_prompt: Watch measurement, estimate, and decision as separate ROBOT evidence. Press L for estimated LiDAR projection, E for estimate, and T for deterministic Turbo.

lessons: Sensors provide measurements; perception and localization build estimates from them.
ROBOT completion and SIM truth arrival are checked separately.
Collision is a hard failure. Speed, smoothness, or energy cannot compensate for it.
